newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher in dull trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Thursday in thin trading with traders saying the market was looking for direction amid political uncertainty.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.58 percent, or 1.46 points, to 252.76 on low all-share turnover of 76 million shekels against 80 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.62 percent higher at 261.74.

"The market rose sharply at the beginning of the week, then it consolidated and now it's ready to start rising again. The only thing that prevents the market from rising is the political uncertainty," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
Ilan Doron, head of trading at Solid Financial Markets, said the market was looking for direction.
"The rise of the dollar and falling bond yields are good indicators for the stock market, but the political situation prevents the market from rising," Doron said.
Israeli troops on Thursday again clashed with Palestinian stone-throwers in West Bank street battles triggered by a Jewish housing project in Arab East Jerusalem.
Scharia added that the slowing economy would lead the Bank of Israel to lower its key lending rate.
"A rate cut will push the market upwards. If the peace process continues, the outlook for the market is very positive," he added.
Doron predicted the central bank was unlikely to cut rates in the short term: "We predict that the rate will remain unchanged at least for the next two months."
Both traders noted that volume was relatively low as investors wait for further political developments to salvage Middle East peace moves.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim, which gained 1.0 percent to 697 on volume of 3.8 million shekels; Koor Industries, which fell 0.75 percent to 30,899 agorot on a turnover of 3.4 million shekels; and Israel Chemicals, which rose 3.25 percent to 392 agorot on volume of 3.3 million shekels.
